pages.text: Soft snow fell all morning, piling up fluffily in the yard. Momo hopped across it.
"I'll make a snowman." Grandma opened the window and looked out. "I'll make it later," Yuki said.
Yuki drew pictures inside. Before long, the snow stopped. "I'll make it this evening."
At dinner, the window showed growing darkness. "I'll make it tomorrow morning."
Wind blew hard at night. The snow's surface became smooth and shiny.
In the morning, Yuki squeezed a handful of snow. It crumbled apart.
No amount of squeezing made a round ball. Only Yuki's hands grew cold. "Why won't it stick together?"
Grandma tried rolling a snowball. The snow kept crumbling. "Put snow off until morning, and it turns to stone."
A few days later, snow fell again. Yuki went straight outside. "Today, I'll make it now!"
Snow stuck snugly in Yuki's hands. A snowman stood taller than Yuki in the yard. "It's taller than me!"
